title: Tone mapping curves pass: clamp, Reinhard, ACES fit and Hable
purpose: Bring a three.js HDR frame into [0, 1] with exposure and a curve chosen at run time (clamp, extended Reinhard with a white point, the Narkowicz ACES fit or the Hable filmic curve), as a ShaderPass definition or full-screen ShaderMaterial with an exact CPU mirror of every curve.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE (the shader includes the colorspace_fragment chunk and an int uniform); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial
contract.renderer_setting: renderer.toneMapping = THREE.NoToneMapping, so the curve is applied once

options.meaning: Linear multiplier applied before the curve.

options.name: whitePoint
options.meaning: Extended Reinhard: the exposed value that maps to 1.

limits: Each curve acts on every channel separately, so saturated highlights shift hue toward the primaries; there is no luminance-only mode, gamut mapping or AgX. The ACES curve is Narkowicz's single rational fit, not the full ACES reference rendering transform, and no 0.6 input scale is applied (use exposure). The Hable parameters are fixed at the published values. The input must keep values above 1 (a HalfFloat or Float target) and three.js's own tone mapping must be off, or the curve applies twice. Output goes through three.js's output colour space conversion. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Extended Reinhard operator with a white point
Narkowicz 2015 rational fit of the ACES filmic curve
Hable filmic curve (shoulder, linear section, toe) normalized by its white point
